what: The YouTube Chapters Generator helps you write the timestamp list that turns into chapters in the YouTube player. Enter a time and a title for each part of your video and it builds a list ready to paste into your description.

It checks the rules YouTube needs before it shows chapters: the first chapter starts at 0:00, there are at least three chapters, each lasts at least 10 seconds, and the times go in order. Problems are shown in plain words, and one click sorts the list.
It also includes a timestamp link maker, so you can share a link that starts a video at an exact moment. Everything runs in your browser.
uses: Add chapters to tutorials, reviews, podcasts and vlogs so viewers can jump to parts.
Fixing chapters that do not show
Check an existing list against YouTube's rules and see exactly what is wrong.
Organise hour-long recordings with h:mm:ss times.
Make a link that starts the video at the exact second you want to show someone.
Split lessons into topics so students can find and rewatch a section.
tutorial: Type the length in "Video length", for example 12:45. This lets the tool check the last chapter is at least 10 seconds long and no chapter is past the end.
The first row starts at 0:00. Type a time in m:ss or h:mm:ss and a short title in each row. Press Enter to move to the next row or add a new one.
Click "+ Add chapter" for more rows, × to remove one, and "Sort by time" to put them in order.
Open "Paste an existing list instead", paste lines such as "1:24 - Unboxing", and click "Load these chapters". The time can be anywhere on the line.
Green ticks show rules that pass; red crosses show what to fix, such as a chapter shorter than 10 seconds.
Click "Copy chapters" and paste the list on its own lines in your video description in YouTube Studio, then save.
In the Timestamp link maker, paste the video link, type a start time and copy the full or short link.
features: First at 0:00, at least 3 chapters, each at least 10 seconds, ascending, no duplicates, nothing past the end.
Accepts m:ss, mm:ss, h:mm:ss or plain seconds.
Reads existing lists with dashes, brackets or other separators.
Full watch?v=…&t= links and short youtu.be links with ?t=.

example.title: Worked example: a 12-minute phone review
example.text: You type 12:40 as the video length and fill in: 0:00 Intro, 0:45 Design, 3:10 Screen, 6:30 Camera, 10:05 Battery, 12:35 Verdict. The checks show a red cross: "Verdict" is only 5 seconds before the end. You change it to 11:50, all checks turn green, and you click "Copy chapters" and paste the list into your YouTube description.

tips: Keep titles short, under about 40 characters, so they fit in the player's progress bar.
Put the chapter list on its own lines; other text can go above or below it.
Use chapters of a sensible length. Many short chapters make the progress bar hard to use.
After saving, it can take a few minutes for chapters to appear on the video.
YouTube may also generate automatic chapters; your own list in the description takes priority.
problems: Chapters do not show on my video
Make sure every check is green, the list is in the description (not a comment), and each line starts with the time. Chapters can also be unavailable on some videos, such as ones marked for kids.
YouTube needs a chapter at the very start. Add a row with 0:00, for example "Intro".
"Each chapter must be at least 10 seconds long"
Two times are too close together, or the last chapter is too close to the end. Move or remove the short chapter.
Use a colon between parts, like 4:05 or 1:02:30. Seconds and minutes must be below 60.
